Definition: to associate; by implication, to overshadow (by huddling together)
BiblicalUsage: To associate, to overshadow by huddling together, and the prophets use it for the tree and the gold. The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him, Ezekiel says of Pharaoh, nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty; and Jeremiah asks, How is the gold become dim, how is the most fine gold changed? The word is the overshadowing and the dimming both at once.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for overshadowing carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two pictures, that the greatest tree in God's garden could not hide Pharaoh and the finest gold can go dim.
